messages:
incident-bot: SEV alert — elevated 5xx rate on inference-runtime-prod (model-runner). Paging oncall @sara. Error rate spike started ~5m ago, 30% 5xx across requests, timeouts increasing. Logs indicate repeated segfaults/OOM on model-runner pods. https://ops.redwood/alerts/INC-212345

sara: I’m on it. paging P1. putting a note in the SEV channel. anyone seeing customer-facing errors? :eyes:

arjun: seeing 502/504 cascade from gateway -> model-runner. stack: lots of `runtime: invalid memory address` and `signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)` on GPU-backed pods. attaching tail of runner logs:

```

2024-08-12T14:02:12Z runner[pid=1243] INFO model_load: quantized init ok
2024-08-12T14:02:17Z runner[pid=1243] ERROR inference: segfault at 0x0
2024-08-12T14:02:17Z runner[pid=1243] ERROR stack: goroutine 1 [running]:
  runtime.throw({0x7f, 0x0})
  ...
2024-08-12T14:02:18Z runner[pid=1243] INFO supervisor: pod restart (reason: segfault)
2024-08-12T14:02:19Z runner[pid=1251] ERROR inference: OOM trying to allocate 4200MB
```

mike: those restarts are thrashing the pool. k8s restart loops + warming model -> gateway sees 502/504. pattern looks like a specific kernel/quant path -> segfault then heavy allocs on restart leading to OOM.

liz: which model? I’m seeing it for `redwood/gptx-3b-quant` on seq_len 1024 requests. small fraction of requests with long context trigger larger allocation.

arjun: confirmed. failing pods are all on GPU nodes with driver 525.x and using optimized attention kernels. hypothesis: a kernel regression in the optimized path hitting particular batch shape.

infra-bot: telemetry: 17 pods crashed in last 6m, affected AZ us-west-2b primarily. Node gpu-azb-12 reported GPU memory ECC errors ~14:58 UTC.

sara: mitigate plan — short term: reduce traffic to the affected model variant and route to fallback CPU-quant variant; lower batch size and reject long-context (>512) requests with 429/slowdown; disable optimized-kernel flag on runner config for canary nodes. who can push routing?

mike: I can flip a route to redirect 60% of traffic to `gptx-3b-quant-fallback` via the traffic-router service. command: 

```
# promote fallback for 60% of traffic
curl -X POST https://router.internal/v1/routes/promote -d '{"model":"gptx-3b-quant-fallback","pct":60}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN"
```

mike: also lowering batch/seq limits on the runtime: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/model-runner --all BATCH_MAX=4 SEQ_MAX=512
```

liz: canary suggestion: spin up 2 model-runner instances with optimized-kernel disabled: `RUNTIME_KERNELS=generic` then route 10% to them to validate.

arjun: doing that now. disabling optimized kernels on two pods. logs show they start and accept requests (no segfault so far).

```
# runtime env for canary
kubectl -n inference patch deploy runner-canary -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runner","env":[{"name":"RUNTIME_KERNELS","value":"generic"},{"name":"BATCH_MAX","value":"4"}]}]}}}}'
```

jess: support: we have ~8 active customer sessions reporting failures via support chat. Current estimate: ~0.9% of total users impacted but concentrated on high seq workloads (labs + research accounts). I’ve opened a customer-impact doc and pinged CS leads.

sara: good. declare SEV-1, notify execs, and add status page note forthcoming. timeline: mitigations in progress — routing change and canary disable. objective: reduce 5xx to <1% within 15m.

infra-bot: action taken: route change deployed (60% fallback), batch limits set, 2 canary runners patched. Observed 5xx rate drop to 12% within 3m.

arjun: digging into core dumps — minimal symbols but binary trace points to `attention_kernel_optimized` function. reproducing locally with a minimal repro: varying batch/seq shapes triggers segfault in op with specific CUDA kernel launch params. possible bad kernel launch checks (missing bounds check) -> segfault.

mike: immediate next step: keep fallback route and scale fallback pool x2, keep canary disabled kernels running. plan to push a hotfix to runtime to guard kernel callsite (safe-fallback) and disable optimized kernels cluster-wide if hotfix risks high.

sara: if hotfix ETA > 1hr, plan B: keep fallback routing and lower overall concurrency temporarily and notify customers of degraded throughput. who takes next 1hr oncall? I need a handoff at +45m.

arjun: I’ll own the hotfix patch. rough ETA 35-50m including build + rollout to canary. I’ll post PR link when ready.

liz: until patch is in, I recommend trimming sequence lengths at API layer for the variant and surface a clear error message so customers can retry with shorter contexts.

jess: notifying affected customers with interim mitigation and ETA. will keep support-runbook updated.

mike: monitoring: dashboard shows 5xx down to 6% after route + limits. latency for fallback higher by ~120ms but acceptable.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: SEV-1 assigned to oncall:sara, responders: arjun, mike. Runbook: https://ops.redwood/runbooks/inference-sev

sara: ok prepping handoff. next-oncall @oliver you’ll take +45m if unresolved. tag me if you need escalation.

oliver: ack, will be ready to take over. please add notes to the incident doc and the postmortem checklist.

arjun: PR posted: https://git.internal/rw/runner/commit/patch-kernguard-234 — patch adds boundary checks and fallback to generic kernel on error. deploying to canary now.

arjun: canary rollout shows no segfaults after 12m and stable memory. merging and preparing staged rollout (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with 5m wait windows.

sara: great. leaving detailed notes in the incident doc. summarizing customer impact: ~0.9% of users experienced errors, primarily in high-context workloads. mitigation: traffic reroute to fallback, batch/seq limits, kernel disable canary, patch deployment in progress. next steps: full rollout of patch, postmortem + root cause analysis, deliver customer communication.

jess: support will send follow-ups to affected customers once patch is fully rolled out.

incident-bot: SEV updated: status=mitigated (partial), assigned=arjun, next-update=+30m.

sara: handing over to @oliver in 30m. leaving channel to grab lunch briefly — call me if it spikes again. :coffee:

oliver: I’ve got it. monitoring alerts subscribed. will escalate if 5xx >2% or restarts resume.

[reaction :thumbsup: from arjun]
